primary_meaning: Spiritual uncleanness, hardness of heart, or exclusion from God's covenant people (contrasted with the need for heart-circumcision)
primary_basis: Genesis 17:10-14 (physical circumcision as covenant sign; uncircumcised as cut off)
Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4; Jeremiah 9:25-26 (call to circumcise the heart; judgment on the uncircumcised in heart)
Romans 2:25-29 (true circumcision is of the heart by the Spirit)
Ephesians 2:11-12; Colossians 2:11 (uncircumcision of the flesh vs. circumcision of Christ putting off the body of flesh)

alternatives.meaning: The sinful flesh or carnal nature that must be put off in conversion/union with Christ
Ethnic/religious outsiders (Gentiles or non-covenant peoples) as opposed to Jews
Impediment or unfitness for speech/service (uncircumcised lips)

notes: Christian biblical interpretation consistently treats physical foreskin/uncircumcision as a type pointing to spiritual realities of impurity, unbelief, or covenant status, with the NT emphasizing heart-circumcision over the physical rite. No major competing symbolic systems displace this reading in mainstream teaching.
